chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked: What is the minimum right of a believer upon his brother?
He replied: That he does not monopolize for himself what the other needs more than he does.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum right of a believer upon another believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the baseline of social equity by prohibiting the hoarding of essentials that a brother requires more than the owner, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *haqq al-nas* (rights of people). This principle extends beyond mere charity to a structural obligation of resource distribution, ensuring that wealth circulates to meet urgent needs rather than accumulating in the hands of those for whom it is less critical.
